chapter: The Dallas nightclub and Jesse Stone's band
title: Dice game with the boss; the apartment at 13th and Lydia
summary: Stone wins the boss's money, the band is fired and moves to an apartment at 13th and Lydia in Kansas City.

story.theme_name: Playing with Count Basie: joining, leading, leaving
story.community_name: Playing with Count Basie: the band, its feel and its people

blocks.x: Now, in Kansas City they had -- well, of this -- as I told you, we were working in Dallas, Missouri, and we used to come into Kansas City on weekends, and whatnot, and get our haircuts, and whatnot, and try to meet the musicians. So finally, one night we got in a dice game with the boss, at Dallas, Missouri, and --

That's this place were we were working for tips. And Jesse Stone is still in shock. He broke the boss, which is about three hundred something dollars. The boss said look, you can't quit now, and he said I'll put up the keys to my car. Jesse said, 'Oh no. I couldn't do that.' He says, 'You can't do that? Well then you're fired.'
So we had to get out. So we came into Kansas City,
and we went ________ place. We found an apartment on 13th and Lydia. I never will forget that, because I --

Yes. 13th and Lydia, and I wrote a tune and called it '13th and Lydia,' and when Booker Pittman came from South America later we recorded that for Columbia. I don't know whether they ever put it out, but this guy Frank Drake that wrote some of this stuff, recorded us.

Anyway, we went into this apartment, and we took this money, and we paid for the apartment. We didn't even have no sheets, no -- you know, nothing. We all crowded in this apartment, went out to the store and brought up a lot of cheese and crackers and everything, so we could make it, but really we didn't have nothing, you know. We were just there, and we tried to proceed to get work.
